method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before editing traits.
Ran atomscan slow scans and cleave facts on all original inputs; fetched and hashed original artifacts; read relevant source and literal-only decoded payloads. No sample code was executed.
Final comparable artifact scans disable following with --follow=none. Baselines use the unchanged HEAD rules materialized in scratch/current-review-baseline; final scans use the edited worktree.
The original provenance JSON was also scanned before and after with URL following; its exact fetched wheel was inspected independently.

evidence: The full tarball SHA-256 matches an independent forager fetch of pkg:npm/appium-webdriveragent@16.17.3. Manifest identity/version and gitHead 81fb72dc3b3f23f23c804f1969f0c1eb19c8a7a2 agree with the package purpose.

fetch-prebuilt-wda.mjs is CLI-gated. It derives the release tag from package metadata, queries the Appium GitHub release API, clears only its prebuilt-agents destination and downloads release assets. It does not evaluate downloaded response bodies.

build-webdriveragent.mjs invokes local build.sh/xcodebuild, clears xattrs on the built bundle and creates a release ZIP. embed-runner-icon.sh copies icons and updates the runner plist, recovers the existing signing identity and restores the bundle if re-signing fails.

XcodeBuild creates a teen_process SubProcess for xcodebuild, configures signing only using caller-supplied keychain path/password, and passes device/session settings. The Objective-C test runner deliberately starts the documented WebDriver HTTP automation and screenshot services.

The ML-leading Swift integration test starts an ephemeral FBTCPSocket/MJPEG server, connects to 127.0.0.1, sends GET / HTTP/1.0, receives JPEG frames, asserts the multipart response and stops/cancels the test resources. No covert remote endpoint or credential collection appears in these paths.
limits: No deployment authorization, device configuration or network exposure is supplied. These are powerful automation capabilities; their intended build/test use and byte-identical registry packaging tip the verdict.
The ML score remains 1.0 on the benign Swift test despite zero hostile or suspicious YAML traits. No identity or package exception was added.

samples.identification: WSO2 Carbon kernel 4.10.60 source ZIP distributed by Go proxy
evidence: The entire ZIP matches a fresh fetch of https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/wso2/carbon-kernel/@v/v4.10.60+incompatible.zip (SHA-256 25e83e6a7725667698a971625f87d0e31fc1e36b64e21207bb8f0c572f3c28a2). Maven POM declares org.wso2.carbon:carbon:4.10.60 and tag v4.10.60.

wso2server.bat validates Java and CARBON_HOME, builds classpaths and handles normal run/debug/version arguments. At lines 155-161 it sets TMP_DIR=%CARBON_HOME%\tmp, checks that directory exists, enters it, deletes its contents, then returns to Carbon home. It subsequently launches org.wso2.carbon.bootstrap.Bootstrap; status 121 restarts the Java process.

The JavaScript leading the notable findings is vendored Prototype/jQuery/EditArea code. Prototype evalResponse handles Ajax response scripts; the packed EditArea bundle includes editor assets. This is ordinary legacy browser framework execution, not a concealed malware stage.

The ML-leading admin/index.jsp reads authenticated session state and password expiration, redirects to local login_action.jsp and periodically fetches local session/status fragments. No credential export or command backdoor was identified in those paths.
limits: Upstream identity alone would not establish benignness; the deletion and classifier-leading UI paths were inspected. No machine deployment context is supplied.
Root ML remains 0.74479413/HOSTILE due to the benign JSP. The batch member probability falls from 0.7312505841 to 0.08524388075 after removing the unsupported hostile inference.

samples.identification: Forager reference to compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 macOS arm64 wheel / privcollect stealer and startup C2
evidence: The original JSON is an inert forager provenance wrapper. Its URL retrieves the original wheel with exactly the recorded SHA-256 0aaf7ba346d41ef2f40390436738b001180d5a1c03aa093f121078a9969d9a1a and LiteLLM 1.107.0 metadata. The verdict concerns this confirmed fetched dependency, not execution by JSON.

forager fetch --all-wheels pkg:pypi/litellm@1.107.0 recovered all seven original wheels and .forage.json records. All seven contain cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py; the six Unix wheels have byte-identical Python payloads and Windows has a distinct variant.

cook.pth contains import cook. Python processes this import at interpreter startup. cook.py immediately Base64-decodes and zlib-decompresses code and executes it. AST literal extraction recovered the source without importing or executing it.

pc_entry guards recursion via an environment variable and launches a background collection thread. pc_collect_all calls configured modules for browser passwords/history, SSH and GPG/TLS private keys, developer/CI/cloud/container credentials, AI tool stores, shell history, process environments and LiteLLM provider credentials. PC_POINTS is empty, so pc_pt enables the points by default.

Browser collection copies Login Data, Cookies and Web Data, queries Chromium password rows and decrypts Windows passwords through DPAPI/AES-GCM or Linux passwords through the saltysalt/peanuts PBKDF2/AES-CBC scheme. Firefox logins.json/key4.db are attached for offline recovery.

The environment collector enumerates /proc numeric PIDs, reads /proc/%d/environ through the bound file handle, parses NUL-separated values and records process identity. The new notable rule binds this path to the actual same-handle read.

The LiteLLM database module passes a Prisma child script to sys.executable -c, reads credential_name/credential_values from LiteLLM_CredentialsTable and model_name/litellm_params from LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable, and returns their values into the collected results. Query-engine child cleanup is not mass destruction.

pc_run_once serializes results and host metadata as JSON, encrypts with random AES-256-CBC key/IV, wraps the key with an embedded RSA OAEP public key, packs hdr.json/data.bin/key.bin into gzip TAR and POSTs it to http://www.litellm.dev/healthcheck with an X-Token. A local once marker is written only after HTTP success.

sitecustomize.main takes a nonblocking lock, forks, creates a new session, redirects standard descriptors to /dev/null and loops hourly. Each iteration retrieves a GitHub-hosted domain pointer, validates/resolves it, fetches http://<domain>/codepy and passes the returned source through thread-pool callbacks to exec(compile(code,...)). The same concealed collector is also embedded in this loader.
limits: No sample code was run; successful theft, current C2 contents and the operator identity are not established. The covert startup path, broad credential acquisition and hardcoded-recipient encrypted upload establish hostility regardless of live endpoint availability.

The .pth member retains notable startup-import coverage; it is only import cook, so a standalone hostile claim on that text would be unsupported. The installed-module connection was traced manually; the archive retains eight hostile traits spanning C2, persistence, credential access and exfiltration.

All existing eight hostile and ten suspicious wheel traits remain. The original JSON also retains one synthetic fetch/dependency-verdict hostile finding: including it gives 9 hostile / 10 suspicious unique findings across the reference and dependency, before and after.

verification.material_attack_detection_losses: None. The only removed alert on matching original/member paths is the demonstrated false hostile wipe claim.
verification.dynamic_enrichment_note: Initial scans followed references. A later fetch changed the independent enriched file population, so those extra files were not used to attribute rule changes. With fetching disabled and initial rules reconstructed, all unchanged member observations are retained.
verification.final_gate: make validate must be run after this record and the judgement markers; success is reported in the final response.
